summary: HB 1156 (2023, K-12 facilities) extended 2025. School-focused, so traveler exposure is narrower than in adult-reaching bans. In the worst-law group per the July 2026 legal-risk assessment. Below the national score 0.36.

sources.summary: MAP (Movement Advancement Project) equality-map page cataloguing state bans on transgender people's use of public bathrooms and facilities according to their gender identity; the dossier cites it (via its Feb 2026 citations PDF, also 404 at fetch time) for HB 1156 as a 2023 K-12 facility ban extended in 2025. NOTE: URL returned a 404 at fetch time (MAP has moved the page).

Erin In The Morning, 'Anti-Trans National Legal Risk Assessment Map: July 2026' (Stonewall News, published 27 Aug 2026): a per-state legal-risk grading of anti-trans law. The adult map lists 'Do Not Travel (FL, ID, KS, TX)' and 'The Worst States (AL, AR, IA, IN, LA, MS, OH, OK, ND, SC, SD, TN, UT, WV, WY)' - this state is in the worst group. The update records Idaho's promotion to 'Do Not Travel' as the fourth such state after its felony bathroom ban (up to 5 years; partially court-blocked but in force wherever no gender-neutral option exists), Kansas's bounty-hunter civil-suit regime, and a national frame of 'Worst Policies In Effect'.
